zh.summary: 設計能找到問題、保留進度並回到任務的錯誤處理，並以鍵盤、文字標籤與實際任務檢查可近用性。
objectives: 區分資料缺漏、程式失敗與結果過期的復原方式。
為欄位標籤、焦點、鍵盤與非顏色提示寫出待驗條件。
保留自動檢查、人工操作與真人易用性測試各自的證據範圍。

readingGuide.goal: 區分資料缺漏、程式失敗與結果過期的復原方式。
readingGuide.startingPoint: 先用四狀態草圖；有自己的本機原型或教師示範環境後，再用瀏覽器與鍵盤操作。未啟動原型不填實測結果。
readingGuide.route: 先看情境與原理，再比較例子，最後擴寫 wireframe-notes.md 並用檢核題自查。
readingGuide.output: 具有復原設計及如實區分草圖、鍵盤實測與待驗項目的 wireframe-notes.md。

sections.heading: 出錯後，如何繼續完成工作？
paragraphs: 這一課的核心觀念：好的軟體，不是永遠不會出錯，而是出錯之後，使用者仍然知道發生什麼事、如何修正，以及怎麼繼續完成工作。
本課對應 CS Kairos Learn｜M04-06 原始教材。我們會用電商、醫院、銀行、政府服務與 AI 軟體等不同情境來理解。
你需要掌握三個概念：

1. 錯誤復原（Error Recovery）：出問題時，能不能修正並繼續工作？
2. 可近用性（Accessibility）：不同能力、不同操作方式的人，能不能使用這套系統？
3. 易用性（Usability）：使用者能不能有效率、少困惑地完成原本的目標？
這三個概念彼此有關，但不是同一回事。

sections.heading: 一、錯誤復原：別讓使用者的努力白費
paragraphs: 想像你在政府網站填寫一份補助申請書。
你已經花了 25 分鐘填寫個人資料、家庭收入、銀行帳號，以及上傳證明文件。
最後按下「送出」，網站卻顯示：

blocks.caption: 圖 1｜無法繼續工作的失敗訊息
blocks.description: 反例：只有失敗與重填要求，沒有說明缺漏、保留狀態或下一步。靜態示範，非真實系統。

items.title: 發生錯誤
items.body: 系統處理失敗，請重新填寫所有資料。

items.title: 觀察問題
items.body: 使用者不知道哪裡出錯，也不知道先前工作是否保留。

paragraphs: 這是一種很糟糕的設計。
問題不只在於系統出錯，而是使用者不知道自己錯在哪裡，甚至可能失去先前所有工作成果。
較好的設計應該是：

blocks.caption: 圖 2｜能繼續申請的復原訊息
blocks.description: 正例：明確指出缺件、保留其他資料，並提供可執行的下一步。示範訊息，非真實系統。

items.title: 尚未完成申請
items.body: 你尚未上傳「收入證明文件」。

items.title: 保留進度與下一步
items.body: 其他資料都已保留，請補上收入證明後，再按「重新檢查」。

paragraphs: 這裡有一個重要的設計公式：

blocks.caption: 圖 3｜好的錯誤復原
blocks.description: 三個要素以加號相連，表示共同條件，不代表三個依序發生的畫面。

items.title: 指出問題
items.body: 具體說明哪裡需要修正。

items.title: 保留進度
items.body: 保留已完成且可安全保留的工作。

items.title: 提供下一步
items.body: 說明補填、重新檢查、重試或求助的動作。

blocks.heading: 1. 三種錯誤，必須有三種處理方法
paragraphs: 以下以合成情境說明設計與驗證。
教材特別強調，不是所有錯誤都應該顯示同樣的訊息。

blocks.caption: 表 1
rows: 保留資料，說明失敗並提供適當重試或求助
原來的檢查結果已經不符合新資料
取消舊結果有效狀態，要求重新檢查

paragraphs: 例如在銀行貸款申請系統中：
情境 A：沒有填寫月收入。 系統應告訴你缺少月收入，而不是清空姓名、地址與其他資料。
情境 B：銀行伺服器暫時無法連線。 系統應說明本次查詢未完成，讓你在恢復連線後重試；如果是付款或正式交易，重試前還必須避免重複提交。
情境 C：已經通過貸款資格試算，但你後來把月收入從 8 萬改成 5 萬。 原本「符合資格」的結果可能已經失效。系統不能繼續將舊結果顯示為有效，必須要求重新計算。
第三種錯誤特別重要，因為它不一定會讓程式當掉，卻可能讓使用者根據過期資料做出錯誤決策。

sections.heading: 二、可近用性：不是每個人都用同樣的方式操作電腦
paragraphs: Accessibility（可近用性，也常稱無障礙設計）最重要的問題是：
如果使用者不能看清楚畫面、無法使用滑鼠、辨識顏色有困難，或需要輔助科技，他還能不能完成任務？
這不只關乎身心障礙者。
例如，醫師可能戴著手套操作醫療設備；工廠員工可能在強光或吵雜環境中使用系統；高齡者可能需要放大文字；工程師也可能因滑鼠故障而只能使用鍵盤。

blocks.heading: 1. 錯誤不能只靠顏色表達
paragraphs: 以下以合成情境說明設計與驗證。
想像電商結帳頁面有三個欄位，其中一欄填錯了。

- 不好的設計：只把錯誤欄位變成紅色。
- 較好的設計：顯示紅色邊框、錯誤圖示，以及「郵遞區號格式不正確，請輸入三碼或五碼」等符合實際規則的文字。郵遞區號長度依服務與地區規則設定，三碼或五碼只是原稿示例。
原因是顏色可以幫助辨認，但不能是唯一的資訊來源。這也是 WCAG 2.2 的 1.4.1 Use of Color 所要求的方向。
實際設計參考：美國 CMS Design System 的表單錯誤處理

blocks.caption: 圖 4｜表單錯誤摘要與欄位提示
blocks.description: 依 CMS Design System 附圖重製的靜態教學示意；摘要連到本圖問題欄位。範例姓名長度與 MM/DD/YYYY 是示例規則，非所有服務通則。

items.title: 1｜頁首錯誤摘要
items.body: 請完成以下項目以建立帳號：

items.title: 2a｜姓氏
items.body: 請輸入超過 1 個字元的姓氏。

items.title: 2b｜出生日期
items.body: 請以 MM/DD/YYYY 輸入出生日期。

items.title: 已填名字
items.body: Lisa

items.title: 3｜姓氏欄位提示
items.body:
請輸入超過 1 個字元的姓氏。
目前值：空白

items.title: 出生日期欄位提示
items.body:
請以 MM/DD/YYYY 輸入出生日期。
月：空白／日：01／年：1990

items.title: 4｜送出位置
items.body: 靜態示意；此處不送出資料。

paragraphs: design.cms.gov
圖中同時使用頁首錯誤摘要、連到問題欄位的連結，以及欄位旁的文字提示。不是只有紅框。來源：CMS Design System。

blocks.heading: 2. 不使用滑鼠，也必須能完成工作
paragraphs: 以下以合成情境說明設計與驗證。
假設醫院的掛號網站可以使用滑鼠操作所有功能，但如果改用鍵盤，就會遇到這些問題：

- 可以按 Tab 移動，但無法選擇門診日期。
- 可以進入日期選擇器，卻無法離開。
- 不知道目前鍵盤選中了哪個按鈕。
- 按下 Enter 無法完成確認。
這些都是鍵盤可近用性的問題。
認識幾個重要操作：

blocks.caption: 表 2
rows: 移動到下一個可聚焦元件
啟動按鈕、連結等適用元件
操作按鈕、核取方塊等適用元件
關閉某些對話框、選單等元件

paragraphs: 實際按鍵行為會依元件類型而不同。
還有一個關鍵名詞叫做 Focus（焦點）。
焦點就是鍵盤目前準備操作的元件。你可以把它想像成「現在輪到誰接收命令」。
如果焦點不明顯，使用者就像在黑暗中按電梯按鈕，不知道下一步會發生什麼。
W3C 的 WCAG 要求相關功能能透過鍵盤操作，並提供可辨識的焦點指示；少數本質依賴連續移動軌跡的操作則有特定例外。

blocks.heading: 3. 標籤不只是畫面上的文字
paragraphs: 以下以合成情境說明設計與驗證。
這裡涉及兩個經常混淆的概念：
視覺關係：文字看起來位於輸入框旁邊。
程式關係：系統實際知道這段文字就是該輸入框的名稱。
例如：

blocks.heading: HTML｜標籤與錯誤關聯
paragraphs: 保留原稿程式碼；這是語意片段，不代表已完成可近用驗收。
blocks.code: 請輸入有效的電子郵件地址

paragraphs: 白話解釋：

- `label`：告訴使用者這個欄位是什麼。
- `for` 與 `id`：把文字標籤和輸入框正式連起來。
- `aria-describedby`：把補充說明或錯誤訊息關聯到欄位。
- `aria-invalid`：指出目前輸入值無效。
這些關聯可以幫助螢幕閱讀器（Screen Reader）等輔助科技理解表單；但是，有寫 ARIA 不代表一定可近用，仍然必須測試實際操作與訊息宣告。

sections.heading: 三、易用性：能操作，不代表好操作
paragraphs: Accessibility 和 Usability 的差別，可以用航空公司的線上訂票系統理解。
假設一個網站符合主要鍵盤與螢幕閱讀器技術要求，但使用者需要經過 17 個頁面才能改票，甚至不知道哪裡能查看改票費用。
這個網站可能具備某些可近用能力，卻仍然非常難用。

blocks.heading: 用航空改票比較兩種問題
paragraphs: 以同一任務分別檢查可操作與能否順利完成目標。

blocks.caption: 表 3
rows: 不同使用者能不能操作？
鍵盤無法操作日期欄位
正確語意、鍵盤支援、清楚焦點
簡化流程、明確回饋、減少負擔
技術檢測及輔助科技實測
觀察真實使用者執行任務

paragraphs: 兩者不能互相取代。

sections.heading: 四、把錯誤復原設計成一條真正能走完的路
paragraphs: 延續上一節 M04-05 的四種介面狀態：輸入、處理中、缺漏或失敗、完成。現在不只要把畫面畫出來，更要思考不同狀態之間如何安全轉換。
概念流程圖：實際產品可依業務需求增加狀態，例如待審核、已送出、已取消。

blocks.caption: 圖 5｜有分支的復原路徑
blocks.description: 箭頭表示概念狀態轉換；結果判斷後依條件分流，不把失敗當成成功前的必經步驟。修改既有輸入時，舊結果必須重新驗證。

items.title: 輸入資料
items.body: 使用者填寫必要欄位

items.title: 處理中
items.body: 檢查、驗證、計算

items.title: 結果判斷
items.body: 成功、缺漏或技術失敗

items.title: 缺漏或技術失敗 → 需修正／重試
items.body: 保留資料，提供出口；修正後回到輸入／重新檢查。

items.title: 成功 → 完成
items.body: 有效結果與下一步；修改輸入後使舊結果失效。

paragraphs: 以 AI 文件分析系統為例：
使用者上傳一份報告，AI 已經分析完成。接著他把原文件換成新版，但畫面仍然顯示舊版報告的「完成」狀態與下載按鈕。
這不是單純的文字提示問題，而是系統的資料一致性（Data Consistency）問題。
較可靠的設計是讓分析結果綁定輸入版本；輸入變動時，將舊結果標成過期，禁止當成新結果匯出，並由後端再次驗證。這樣即使使用者繞過介面，也不會直接取得錯誤的有效結果。

sections.heading: 五、怎麼證明你的設計真的好用？
paragraphs: 本章另一個非常重要的觀念，是不要把不同層級的證據混在一起。

blocks.caption: 表 4
rows: 有規劃錯誤訊息與復原路徑
找出部分程式語意、對比等問題
特定工具與環境下的體驗
使用者實際在哪裡卡住
所有人都會得到相同結果

paragraphs: 這就是為什麼「Tab 可以走到所有按鈕」不能直接宣稱整個網站符合 WCAG；「五名試用者都完成任務」也不能直接宣稱沒有可近用問題。

blocks.heading: 最小實作練習
paragraphs: 以下以合成情境說明設計與驗證。
你可以任選一個正在設計的系統，例如預約掛號、訂房、論文上傳、AI Agent 操作台，完成下列工作：

1. 畫出輸入、處理中、錯誤、完成四種畫面。
2. 替資料缺漏、技術失敗、結果過期三種情況設計不同的錯誤訊息與復原動作。
3. 設定一條完整任務：「故意漏填 → 修正 → 重新檢查 → 成功 → 修改輸入 → 舊結果失效」。
4. 使用鍵盤重新操作整條流程，確認焦點可見、順序合理、沒有鍵盤陷阱。
5. 把設計預期與實際測試分開記錄到 `wireframe-notes.md`。
真正的驗收標準不是畫面上出現綠色勾勾，而是每一步都有可觀察的結果，系統不會把尚未完成或已過期的工作冒充完成。

sections.heading: 六、理解檢核
paragraphs: 請先回答下面這個整合情境，不必寫程式。
某醫療 AI 網站讓醫師上傳影像後產生分析結果，現在發現三個問題：
問題 A： 上傳時網路中斷，原本填寫的病歷備註全部消失。
問題 B： 使用者可以透過 Tab 選中分析按鈕，但焦點沒有任何視覺提示。
問題 C： 醫師上傳新影像後，仍可下載上一張影像的 AI 分析報告，而且報告被標示為「已完成」。
請回答：

1. A、B、C 分別涉及哪些 UX、Accessibility 或系統正確性問題？
2. 你會怎麼修改三個問題？需要前端、後端，還是兩者共同處理？
3. 如果工程師說「我們已經用自動化工具掃描過，所以通過無障礙驗證」，你會要求補充哪些證據？
完成思考後，展開參考解析核對理由，並把這些觀念連接到下一模組 M05 的規格撰寫，以及 M08 的軟體驗證。

exercise.environment: 先用四狀態草圖；有自己的本機原型或教師示範環境後，再用瀏覽器與鍵盤操作。未啟動原型不填實測結果。
steps: 在草圖上分別標記缺漏、技術失敗與結果過期的訊息、進度保留及回復動作。
若原型可用，將滑鼠放旁邊，以 Tab／Shift+Tab、文字輸入及適合元件的按鍵重演缺件修正；觀察焦點與可離開性。
將實際結果或待驗狀態寫入 wireframe-notes.md，另列輔助科技、真人任務與未覆蓋錯誤；選一項阻礙安排修改與重測。
exercise.expected: 具有復原設計及如實區分草圖、鍵盤實測與待驗項目的 wireframe-notes.md。
exercise.check: 三類問題有不同出口；不把缺少原型時的紙上檢查、單次鍵盤操作或截圖當完整可近用認證。
exercise.cleanup: 只用合成資料，保留環境與重演步驟；不公開非必要個資或未授權錄影。

openChecks.prompt: A、B、C 分別涉及哪些 UX、Accessibility 或系統正確性問題？
answer: A 涉及錯誤復原與 UX：網路中斷造成努力流失。B 是可見焦點與鍵盤可近用問題，可達仍不足以操作。C 是資料一致性與系統正確性問題，也會造成誤導的 UX；報告必須對應正確影像版本。

openChecks.prompt: 你會怎麼修改三個問題？需要前端、後端，還是兩者共同處理？
answer: A 由前端保留安全可保留的輸入，必要時由後端提供受權限與保存期限控制的草稿／復原機制；先確認提交狀態再重試。B 由前端提供清楚的 focus-visible 樣式並實測順序、操作與離開。C 由前後端共同綁定輸入與分析版本：修改後失效，下載時後端再次檢查，不只隱藏按鈕。醫療資料的保留另需符合實際授權與保護規則。

openChecks.prompt: 如果工程師說「我們已經用自動化工具掃描過，所以通過無障礙驗證」，你會要求補充哪些證據？
answer: 要求掃描工具、版本、頁面範圍、日期、報告及修正後重測，另補指定流程的人工鍵盤測試、焦點／錯誤訊息／標籤語意檢查、指定輔助科技與環境實測，以及真人任務觀察。各自寫出覆蓋與待驗，不能以自動掃描或五人成功代表完整 WCAG 合規。

en.summary: Design error handling that locates problems, preserves progress and returns users to their task, then check accessibility through keyboards, text labels and actual tasks.
objectives: Distinguish recovery for missing input, program failure and stale results.
Define pending checks for labels, focus, keyboard operation and non-color feedback.
Retain separate evidence scopes for automated checks, manual operation and actual participant usability tests.

readingGuide.goal: Distinguish recovery for missing input, program failure and stale results.
readingGuide.startingPoint: Begin with four-state sketches. Use a browser and keyboard once your local prototype or a teacher demonstration is available; record no runtime results before starting it.
readingGuide.route: Read the situation and principles, compare examples, then expand wireframe-notes.md and use the checks to review your understanding.
readingGuide.output: wireframe-notes.md with recovery design and honest distinctions among sketches, actual keyboard checks and pending items.

sections.heading: How can users continue after an error?
paragraphs: Good software helps users understand what happened, correct a problem and continue their work after an error.
This lesson expands the M04-06 material through examples from shopping, hospitals, banking, government services and AI software.
You need three concepts:

1. Error recovery: can users correct a problem and continue working?
2. Accessibility: can people with different abilities and ways of operating a system use it?
3. Usability: can users achieve their original goal efficiently and with little confusion?
The concepts are related, but each asks a different question.

sections.heading: 1. Error recovery: preserve the user's effort
paragraphs: Imagine filling out a government subsidy application.
You have spent 25 minutes entering personal details, household income and bank account information, and uploading supporting documents.
You press Submit and see:

blocks.caption: Figure 1 | An error message that stops the task
blocks.description: Counterexample: failure and re-entry are requested without identifying omissions, retained progress or a next action. Static illustration, not a real service.

items.title: An error occurred
items.body: Processing failed. Please enter all information again.

items.title: What is missing?
items.body: Users cannot identify the problem or tell whether earlier work was retained.

paragraphs: This design gives users little help.
They cannot identify what needs correction and may lose all their earlier work.
A more useful design says:

blocks.caption: Figure 2 | Feedback that supports recovery
blocks.description: Identify the missing document, retain other data and provide an actionable next step. Illustrative message, not a real service.

items.title: Application not yet complete
items.body: You have not uploaded the income verification document.

items.title: Retained progress and next action
items.body: All other data has been retained. Upload the income verification document, then select Recheck.

paragraphs: A useful recovery design combines three elements:

blocks.caption: Figure 3 | Good error recovery
blocks.description: Plus signs join three complementary requirements; they do not represent sequential screens.

items.title: Identify the problem
items.body: Explain precisely what needs correction.

items.title: Preserve progress
items.body: Retain completed work that can safely be retained.

items.title: Provide the next action
items.body: Explain completion, rechecking, retry or help.

blocks.heading: Three errors need different responses
paragraphs: The following synthetic scenarios explain design and verification.
Different errors should receive feedback that matches their causes.

blocks.caption: Table 1
rows: Identify the omission and let them complete it
Preserve data, explain the failure and offer appropriate retry or help
An earlier check no longer matches the current input
Withdraw the result's valid status and require a new check

paragraphs: Consider a bank loan application:
Scenario A: monthly income is blank. Identify that omission while keeping the name, address and other values.

Scenario B: the bank server is temporarily unreachable. Explain that this query did not finish and allow a retry after connectivity returns. For a payment or formal transaction, retry must also prevent duplicate submission.
Scenario C: an eligibility estimate passed, but monthly income was then changed from 80,000 to 50,000. The earlier eligible result may no longer apply. Withdraw its valid status and calculate again.
Stale results deserve particular attention: the program may keep running while users make decisions based on outdated information.

sections.heading: 2. Accessibility: people operate computers in different ways
paragraphs: Accessibility asks whether people can complete a task when they cannot see the screen clearly, use a mouse or distinguish colors, or when they need assistive technology.
This includes people who use assistive technology.
These needs also arise in everyday situations.
A doctor may operate equipment while wearing gloves; factory staff may work in bright light or noise; an older person may enlarge text; an engineer with a broken mouse may rely on a keyboard.

blocks.heading: Errors need more than color
paragraphs: The following synthetic scenarios explain design and verification.
Imagine a checkout form with three fields, one of which contains an error.

- A weak design changes only the field's color to red.
- A better design combines a red border, an error icon and wording such as “Postal code format is incorrect; enter three or five digits,” when that matches the service's actual rules. Postal-code length depends on the service and region; three or five digits is only the supplied example.
Color can help recognition, but it must not be the only source of information. WCAG 2.2 criterion 1.4.1, Use of Color, addresses this requirement.
A practical reference is the US CMS Design System's form error pattern:

blocks.caption: Figure 4 | Error summary and field messages
blocks.description: Static teaching adaptation of the supplied CMS Design System example. Summary links target the affected fields in this figure. Surname length and MM/DD/YYYY are example-specific rules.

items.title: 1 | Error summary
items.body: Complete these items to create your account:

items.title: 2a | Last name
items.body: Enter a last name that’s more than 1 character.

items.title: 2b | Date of birth
items.body: Enter birthdate as MM/DD/YYYY.

items.title: Entered first name
items.body: Lisa

items.title: 3 | Last-name field message
items.body:
Enter a last name that’s more than 1 character.
Current value: empty

items.title: Date-of-birth field message
items.body:
Enter birthdate as MM/DD/YYYY.
Month: empty / Day: 01 / Year: 1990

items.title: 4 | Submit position
items.body: Static illustration; no data is submitted here.

paragraphs: The example combines a summary at the top, links to the affected fields and messages beside those fields. It provides information beyond a red outline.
Source: CMS Design System, Error validation. Its surname-length and US date-format rules belong to that example, rather than every service.

blocks.heading: Complete the task without a mouse
paragraphs: The following synthetic scenarios explain design and verification.
A hospital appointment website may work with a mouse yet fail in these keyboard situations:

- Tab moves through the page but cannot select an appointment date.
- The date picker receives focus but cannot be exited.
- There is no visible indication of the currently focused button.
- Enter cannot activate confirmation.
These are keyboard accessibility problems.
Recognize these common keys:

blocks.caption: Table 2
rows: Move to the next focusable component
Activate an applicable button, link or other component
Close certain dialogs, menus or other components

paragraphs: Actual key behavior depends on the component type.
Focus identifies the component ready to receive keyboard input.
It tells you who receives the next command.
Without visible focus, operating a page resembles pressing elevator buttons in the dark without knowing what will happen next.
WCAG requires keyboard operation for relevant functionality and a visible focus indicator. A specific exception concerns functionality inherently dependent on a continuous movement path.

blocks.heading: A label needs a programmatic relationship
paragraphs: The following synthetic scenarios explain design and verification.
Two relationships are easy to confuse:
Visual relationship: text appears beside an input.
Programmatic relationship: the system knows that the text names that input.
For example:

blocks.heading: HTML | Label and error associations
paragraphs: Original source snippet; this does not establish accessibility acceptance.
blocks.code: 請輸入有效的電子郵件地址

paragraphs: The original Chinese code is retained in both editions. The label means “Email” and the message means “Enter a valid email address.”

- label tells users what the field is.
- for and id explicitly connect the label to the input.
- aria-describedby associates additional instructions or an error message with the field.
- aria-invalid indicates that the current input value is invalid.
These relationships help screen readers and other assistive technology interpret the form. Adding ARIA alone does not establish accessibility: test actual operation and message announcements.

sections.heading: 3. Usability: being operable does not ensure a convenient task
paragraphs: An airline booking site illustrates the difference between accessibility and usability.
Suppose it meets major keyboard and screen-reader technical requirements, but changing a ticket takes 17 pages and users cannot find the change fee.
The site may provide some accessible capabilities while remaining difficult to use.

blocks.heading: Compare the two questions through ticket changes
paragraphs: Check both operation and successful goal completion within the same task.

blocks.caption: Table 3
rows: Can they complete their goal smoothly?
A date field cannot be operated by keyboard
The ticket-change process is too complicated
Correct semantics, keyboard support and clear focus
Simpler workflows, clear feedback and less effort

paragraphs: Neither kind of evidence replaces the other.

sections.heading: 4. Design a recovery path users can finish
paragraphs: M04-05 introduced input, processing, missing information or failure, and completion. Now examine how users can move safely between those states.
The conceptual flow can be extended for business needs, such as awaiting review, submitted or cancelled.

blocks.caption: Figure 5 | Recovery with conditional branches
blocks.description: Arrows indicate conceptual state transitions. The decision branches by condition: failure is not required before success. Changing input requires revalidation of old results.

items.title: Input
items.body: The user fills required fields

items.title: Processing
items.body: Check, validate and calculate

items.title: Decision
items.body: Success, missing data or technical failure

items.title: Missing data or technical failure → correct / retry
items.body: Keep data and provide an exit; correction returns to input / rechecking.

items.title: Success → complete
items.body: Valid result and next action; changing input invalidates the old result.

paragraphs: Consider an AI document-analysis system.
A user uploads a report and analysis finishes. They replace the original with a newer version, but the screen still shows the old report as complete and offers its download button.
This is a data-consistency problem as well as a feedback problem.

Bind analysis results to the input version. When input changes, mark earlier results stale, prevent exporting them as current results, and validate the version again on the backend. A user bypassing the interface must not receive an outdated result presented as valid for the new input.

sections.heading: 5. What evidence supports a usable design?
paragraphs: Keep different levels of evidence distinct.

blocks.caption: Table 4
rows: Error messages and recovery paths have been planned
Some semantic, contrast or other defects
The specified operation path was tested
Every user can use the system
Experience with particular tools and environments
Everyone will get the same result

paragraphs: Tab reaching every button does not establish whole-site WCAG conformance. Five participants completing a task does not establish the absence of accessibility problems.

blocks.heading: Minimum practical exercise
paragraphs: The following synthetic scenarios explain design and verification.
Choose a system you are designing, such as hospital appointments, hotel booking, thesis upload or an AI Agent console.

1. Draw input, processing, error and completion screens.
2. Design different messages and recovery actions for missing data, technical failure and stale results.
3. Define a complete task: deliberately omit data → correct it → recheck → succeed → change input → invalidate the old result.
4. Replay the entire path with a keyboard, checking visible focus, sensible order and absence of keyboard traps.
5. Record design expectations separately from actual tests in wireframe-notes.md.
Acceptance requires observable results at each step and accurate status for unfinished or stale work; a green checkmark alone cannot establish that.

sections.heading: 6. Check your understanding
paragraphs: Answer this integrated scenario without writing code.
A medical AI website analyzes images uploaded by doctors. Three problems have been found:
Problem A: a network interruption during upload erases the clinical notes already entered.
Problem B: Tab reaches the analysis button, but focus has no visible indication.
Problem C: after a new image is uploaded, the previous image's AI report remains downloadable and is marked complete.
Answer these questions:

1. Which UX, accessibility or system-correctness problems are involved in A, B and C?
2. How would you fix each problem? Does the fix belong to the frontend, backend or both?
3. An engineer says an automated scan means accessibility verification has passed. What further evidence would you request?
After thinking through your answers, open the reference explanations and compare the reasoning. Connect these ideas to M05 specifications and M08 verification.

exercise.environment: Begin with four-state sketches. Use a browser and keyboard once your local prototype or a teacher demonstration is available; record no runtime results before starting it.
steps: Annotate separate feedback, progress retention and recovery for omissions, technical failure and stale results on the sketch.
If a prototype is available, set the mouse aside. Replay correction with Tab/Shift+Tab, text input and appropriate component keys, observing focus and ability to leave controls.
Record actual results or pending status in wireframe-notes.md. List assistive-technology tests, participant tasks and uncovered errors separately; select one barrier for revision and retesting.
exercise.expected: wireframe-notes.md with recovery design and honest distinctions among sketches, actual keyboard checks and pending items.
exercise.check: The three problems have different exits. Do not treat tabletop review without a prototype, one keyboard path or screenshots as complete accessibility certification.
exercise.cleanup: Use synthetic data only. Keep environment and replay steps; publish no unnecessary personal information or unauthorized recordings.

openChecks.prompt: Which UX, accessibility or system-correctness problems are involved in A, B and C?
answer: A concerns recovery and UX: an interrupted upload destroys prior effort. B concerns visible focus and keyboard accessibility; reachability alone is insufficient. C concerns data consistency and system correctness, while also creating misleading UX. The report must match the correct image version.

openChecks.prompt: How would you fix each problem? Does the fix belong to the frontend, backend or both?
answer: For A, retain input that is safe to retain on the frontend; where needed, provide a backend draft/recovery mechanism with access and retention controls. Confirm submission status before retrying. For B, supply clear focus-visible styling and test order, operation and exits. For C, bind input and analysis versions on both frontend and backend, invalidate results after changes and revalidate downloads on the backend rather than only hiding a button. Medical-data retention also follows actual authorization and protection rules.

openChecks.prompt: An engineer says an automated scan means accessibility verification has passed. What further evidence would you request?
answer: Request the scanning tool/version, page scope, date, report and post-fix retest. Add manual keyboard tests of specified paths, focus/error/label semantics checks, tests with specified assistive technologies and environments, and participant task observations. Record coverage and pending items separately; an automated scan or five successful participants cannot establish complete WCAG conformance.
